description: Collapse many rows into one answer: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, GROUP BY for per-group numbers, and HAVING to filter groups.

screens.body:
Aggregates answer questions about many rows at once: how many students? what's the average GPA? Each aggregate collapses rows into a single number.

The classic five: COUNT (how many), SUM (total), AVG (average), MIN (smallest), MAX (largest). They turn a table into a one-row answer.

options: All the rows as a list
check.question: COUNT(*) answers…

screens.heading: Aggregates collapse rows
screens.keyPoint: Aggregates turn many rows into one number.

screens.body:
COUNT(*) counts every row; COUNT(program) counts only non-empty program values. For simple counting they're the same here — 6 either way.

SUM adds up numbers: SUM of all GPAs is 20.8. AVG divides by the row count: AVG(gpa) is about 3.47. Note AVG ignores NULLs — empty values never drag the average down.

check.question: COUNT(*) and AVG(gpa) on our six students give…

code.snippet:
SELECT COUNT(*), AVG(gpa)
FROM students;
-- returns: 6 | 3.4666...
-- (six GPAs sum to 20.8, /6)

screens.heading: COUNT, SUM, AVG
screens.keyPoint: COUNT counts, SUM totals, AVG averages (ignoring NULLs).

screens.body:
GROUP BY splits rows into groups, then aggregates each one. GROUP BY program with COUNT(*) gives one row per program: Software Development 3, Network Security 2, Data Science 1.

Whatever column you GROUP BY, every other selected column must be aggregated or in the GROUP BY — SQL needs to know which single value to show per group.

options: One row per program with its student count
All six rows with their programs
check.question: SELECT program, COUNT(*) FROM students GROUP BY program returns…

code.snippet:
SELECT program, COUNT(*)
FROM students
GROUP BY program;
-- Software Development | 3
-- Network Security     | 2
-- Data Science         | 1

screens.heading: GROUP BY
screens.keyPoint: GROUP BY = one answer row per group.

screens.body:
WHERE filters rows BEFORE grouping; HAVING filters groups AFTER. Want programs with an average GPA above 3.2? GROUP BY program HAVING AVG(gpa) > 3.2.

Software Development (avg 3.53) and Data Science (3.6) pass; Network Security (2.8) doesn't. You can't use WHERE for this — WHERE doesn't know about averages yet.

code.snippet:
SELECT program, AVG(gpa)
FROM students
GROUP BY program
HAVING AVG(gpa) > 3.2;
-- Software Development | 3.53
-- Data Science         | 3.6

screens.heading: HAVING filters groups
screens.keyPoint: WHERE filters rows first; HAVING filters groups after.

screens.body:
WHERE and GROUP BY work as a team: WHERE filters the rows FIRST, then GROUP BY groups what's left. Count students with GPA 3.0 or higher per program.

Ama (2.9) and Noah (2.4) are filtered out first. Then grouping gives: Software Development 2, Network Security 1, Data Science 1. That's WHERE before groups, HAVING after groups.

check.question: WHERE gpa >= 3.0, then GROUP BY program with COUNT(*):

code.snippet:
SELECT program, COUNT(*)
FROM students
WHERE gpa >= 3.0
GROUP BY program;
-- Software Development | 2 (Ama out)
-- Network Security     | 1 (Noah out)
-- Data Science         | 1

screens.heading: WHERE + GROUP BY together
screens.keyPoint: WHERE shrinks the rows before they group.

screens.body:
MIN and MAX pull out extremes: MIN(gpa) is 2.4 (Noah), MAX(gpa) is 3.9 (Priya). Combined with GROUP BY they give per-group extremes — the top GPA in each program.

MIN/MAX also work on text: MIN(name) would be 'Ama' alphabetically.
screens.heading: MIN and MAX

screens.body:
Read an aggregate query inside out: FROM picks the table, WHERE filters rows, GROUP BY forms the groups, HAVING keeps some groups, SELECT computes the numbers.

In JavaScript you'll do the same with reduce(): build one object with a key per program, accumulating counts and GPA sums as you go.

options: reduce() into an object with a key per program
check.question: In JavaScript, GROUP BY + COUNT is…

code.snippet:
SELECT program, COUNT(*), AVG(gpa)
FROM students
GROUP BY program
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
-- SD: 3 students, avg 3.53
-- NS: 2 students, avg 2.8

screens.heading: Reading an aggregate query
screens.keyPoint: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT.
